Aims
At Brockenhurst CE Primary and Pre-School we will:
Create a nurturing environment founded on Christian values for all
Respect all children, adults, animals and living things
Be vigilant about children’s safety and wellbeing (inc online)
Empower children to overcome barriers to learning
Encourage positive mental wellbeing
Develop resilient, reflective and resourceful learners
Grow critical, creative and evaluative thinkers
Acknowledge, appreciate and celebrate difference and cultural diversity
Utilise the local environment to support learning in a unique setting
Develop confidence through the love and support of the school, church and community

pageCache.pageTitle: Brockenhurst C of E Primary School - Fundamental British Values
pageCache.text:
Fundamental British Values
Inspire a love of learning, within a nurturing Christian environment
FUNDAMENTAL BRITISH VALUES
We actively promote the Fundamental British Values (FBV) and will challenge pupils, staff or parents who express opinions that may be contrary to these.
We encourage learning through the process of exploring, ‘what it means to be British’ and by enabling our pupils to:
We aim to develop a belief in freedom and equality, a respect for the law and for British institutions, tolerance, a belief in personal and social responsibility and a wish to resolve conflict through discussion and democratic procedures.
Our plans for learning, collective worship and other activities, encompass religious tolerance, taking a zero tolerance approach to bullying and violence and the pursuit of excellence in academic and non-academic subjects and pupil wellbeing.
As a school we aim to find enthusiasm for learning and for achievement that stays with the individual as they move on to new challenges and into adulthood.
Underpinning this ethos is a range of curriculum learning that include links to British Values. We celebrate British sports men and women, authors, actors, engineers, artists, designers and scientists and their achievements. Please view the long-term curriculum planning on our school website for more detailed information.
Recognising different identities and experiences;
Appreciating that identity consists of many factors;
Beginning to understand the idea of stereotypes.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brockenhurst C of E Primary School - Church
pageCache.text:
Church
The school has excellent links with Brockenhurst Parish, and particularly St Saviour’s church, which is situated only about half a mile away from the school enabling us to use the church on special occasions such as Harvest, Christmas and Easter.
The Vicar, the Youth Worker and other volunteers from St Saviour’s play, a very active role in helping to embed the school values of Loving, Hopeful and Thankful living in the Christian context through the regular leading of assemblies, classroom and club activities, and events in church.
Several members of the congregation also volunteer and serve as School Governors.
The current Vicar, Revd Simon Newham, describes the link between the school and church as, ‘A great source of joy, encouragement and life, both to the school, the church and to the wider community.’

pageCache.pageTitle: Brockenhurst C of E Primary School - Church Links
pageCache.text:
Church Links
As the Vicar of Brockenhurst I have the privilege and joy of being an ex-officio Foundation Governor for Brockenhurst Primary School. Formally, this means that I work to maintain and support the Christian character and values of the school by attending Governor Meetings, carrying out school visits, meeting with the Head, taking corporate worship both at the school and at the church, going on residential trips and just generally being a resource to the school where and when wanted. Informally, it means making the time to get to know better our wonderful children and staff and the wider school community, as well as praying for them on a regular basis and being a supportive link with the rest of our community. It’s a role I love!
Hi, I’m Mel and I am the Children and Families’ Worker for St Saviour’s Church. Part of my role is to be a bridge between church, school, and home, helping children and families feel supported and connected.
In school, I lead worship and help pupils explore the Bible in creative and fun ways. I also support and encourage a group of Worship Ambassadors to take part in child-led worship and prayer activities. Last year, through a partnership with Christian Aid’s Creative for Climate Justice project, one of our pupils was invited to speak to MPs at a special exhibition of child-created artwork on the theme of Climate Justice. You might also see me around school supporting projects such as intergenerational storytelling, celebrating Christian festivals, or joining in with special events.
Outside of school, I run groups and activities where children and families can have fun, make friends, and discover more about faith together. Everything I do is about creating spaces where people feel valued, welcomed, and able to grow. I love my work and have a heart for building relationships within the community – so do come and say hello if you see me!

Badger's Rest: Breakfast, After School & Holiday Clubs
We offer in-house wrap around care from 7.30am to 6pm with Breakfast and After School Clubs for children attending Brockenhurst Pre-School and Brockenhurst CE Primary School (ages 2-11). Holiday Clubs run for the majority of the school holidays and are bookable via our online payment system, Scopay.
For last minute bookings, please message via Whatsapp: 07752 231977
Breakfast Club runs from 7.30am and includes breakfast for arrivals before 8am. Cost: £5.50 per session.
After-School club runs until 6pm and includes a snack. Cost £12 per session.
Holiday Club runs from 8am to 5pm (children need to bring a nut-free packed lunch). Cost £35 per day, with a £10 discount for siblings.

pageCache.text:
French
Our vision for French:
We believe that learning a foreign language provides an invaluable insight into other cultures. We hope to ignite the children’s curiosity into a new language, to French culture and beyond where the language is used, allowing them to deepen their understanding of the world outside of Brockenhurst. We focus on the key areas of listening, speaking, reading, writing and grammar which are progressed throughout Key Stage 2, providing the children with the key skills to be able to communicate in French and laying the foundations for future learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brockenhurst C of E Primary School - Religious Education (RE)
pageCache.text:
Religious Education (RE)
At Brockenhurst C of E Primary School, we believe the teaching of RE should allow children to explore and reflect on their own way of life and develop an understanding of religious and non-religious ways of living. Through RE lessons, the children should be encouraged to ask questions and recognise that different people respond in different ways to their questions.
We aim to: • Allow children to develop a secure understanding of the Christian faith. • Help the children to learn about and build respect of other religions, understanding differing religious traditions and cultures. • Value and reflect on their own faith and beliefs and introduce them to other faiths within and outside of our community. • Through links with the Church, allow the children the opportunity to experience places of worship. • Progress the children through religious concepts, increasing in complexity throughout their primary education.
